x: Albert Johnson who was with our Eric Hall at the halfway mark, walked a surprisingly fast second half to finish in front of Bob Goodall of Woodford.
By 10 miles he had increased the pace and led in exemplary style by 150 yds from Olympic team mate Albert Johnson of Sheffield; Goodall was a further 200 yds away.

What time Eric would have put up if Albert Johnson the 1956 winner had not been forced to retire is a matter for conjecture, but his performance was all the more meritorious in view of his injury sustained in the match for London v.
They were our own Stan Vickers (was he the Surprise!) and Eric Hall; Met's Don Thompson and Tom Misson (the holder) and Sheffield's Albert Johnson.

From the start, Don Thompson and Tom Misson soon opened up a gap with Albert Johnson of Sheffield close to hand. The two Met. boys over the early stages were closely supported by the other two Thompsons whilst our team, led by Ray Hall, were well spread out over the field.
